claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA is a single-phase BCC alloy.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA has high density.
The baseline alloy has insufficient room-temperature ductility.
Adding a minor amount of V or Cr to Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr will induce a C15 Laves phase.
The proposed C15 phase will be of the Hf2Mo or Hf2Ti type.
A C15 Laves phase has the AB2 structure.
Heat treatment at 450 °C or higher will induce phase separation and stabilize the secondary phase.
The C15 precipitates will form a reticulated network at grain boundaries and within the matrix.
The reticulated Laves network will act as a physical barrier that causes cracks to deflect, branch, or bridge.
Crack deflection, branching, and bridging by the Laves network will dissipate fracture energy and prevent catastrophic brittle failure.
Single-phase BCC RHEAs typically undergo room-temperature brittle failure because of limited slip systems and a lack of crack-arrest mechanisms.
Solid-solution hardening increases yield strength but often reduces ductility.
Adding V or Cr and forming the Laves phase will marginally increase alloy density.
The reticulated Laves phase will significantly improve room-temperature strength-ductility synergy relative to the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will have higher uniform elongation than the baseline alloy.
The beneficial response requires the Laves-phase volume fraction to remain below a percolation threshold for brittleness.
A continuous or semi-continuous Laves network is required for the proposed crack-arrest mechanism.
Isolated coarse Laves particles may embrittle the alloy through particle cracking.
The critical Laves-phase volume fraction separating beneficial crack deflection from detrimental interface crack initiation is unknown for Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
